περί-ζωμα , ατος, τό,
A.girdle worn round the loins,
PRev.Laws 94.7
(iii B. C.), Plu. Rom. 21 (in form περί-ζωσμα ), Poll. 7.65 , etc.; worn by athletes, Paus. 1.44.1 ; by priests, Plu. Aem. 33 ; by smiths, Arr. Epict. 4.8.16 ; ἔχειν π. wear the apron, of a cook, Hegesipp.Com. 1.7 : hence “οἱ λόγοι σου περιζώματος ὄζουσιν”
Plu. 2.182d
; ἀσκεῖν ἐκ περιζώματος practise an art with the apron on. i.e. merely with the outward appendage of an art, superficially, D.H. Din. 1 ; of soldiers, underclothing, ἐν περιζώμασιν, opp. ἐν θώραξι, Plb. 6.25.3 .
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
